angularDiameterSource: Stellar radius 1.11 (+0.15/−0.09) solar radii from Jenkins et al. 2015, AJ 150, 56 (2015). It is a radius from stellar characterisation, not an interferometric diameter; the angular diameter in the record is that radius at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia EDR3 parallax 1.8053 +/- 0.0103 mas via SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G): 553.92 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 1.11 (+0.15/−0.09) solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius, from Jenkins et al. 2015 (AJ 150, 56 (2015); arXiv:1507.06723). GM from their stellar mass 1.037 solar masses times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: no spin axis is measured, so the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 5757 ± 85 K from Jenkins et al. 2015 (AJ 150, 56; https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.06723), Table 2, the radius source: high-resolution spectroscopy with SpecMatch.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the astronomy record's GM and radius (physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; no picture of the photosphere is cast.
